rows.grounds: instrumental of the way of repose in pleasure
state where conceptual thought has departed

items.question: How do people behave when established in awareness beyond conceptualization?
premises: One who attains happiness forgets earlier suffering through resting in happiness.
Likewise, people established in awareness beyond conceptualization do not dwell on conceptual thought.
items.inference: Absorption in non-conceptual awareness naturally displaces conceptual activity, just as present happiness displaces past suffering.
items.plain_english: Just as someone who has found happiness forgets earlier suffering by resting in that happiness, so people who are firmly established in awareness, even when conceptual thought has gone, no longer cling to it.

rows.grounds: power arising from reliance on thought
refers to the non-conceptual state or awareness
do not appropriate or identify with
through the fading away of thought
the becoming manifest of awareness's own nature
in focused attention on that state

items.question: What happens when conceptualization dissolves and one attends to that state?
premises: Those resting on the strength of conceptualization do not claim the non-conceptual state.
Through the dissolution of conceptualization, awareness becomes barren of thought and true in the ultimate sense.
In that condition the manifestness of awareness's own nature is attained.
items.inference: For those who strive with attention, the fading of conceptualization reveals the ultimately true, self-manifest nature of awareness.
items.plain_english: People who rely on conceptual thinking do not lay claim to that deeper state; but when conceptualization dissolves, awareness becomes free of thought and ultimately true, and its own nature shines forth. In this way, clear understanding arises for those who attend to it with effort.

rows.grounds: in the cognition involving object and subject
because it yields the intended result

items.question: What is meant by attentiveness in the relation of grasper and grasped?
premises: There is a relation between the grasped, the grasper, and their awareness.
Attentiveness can be directed within that relation.
Such attentiveness is defined by its connection with the desired result.
items.inference: Attentiveness in the grasper-grasped relation is the focused awareness that brings about the intended fruit.
items.plain_english: This attentiveness is said to occur in the relation between the grasped, the grasper, and their awareness, because in that context it is connected with the attainment of the desired result.

rows.grounds: because of the multiplicity of distinctions within it
and no violation of this principle

items.question: Why do the worlds display such manifold diversity?
premises: The divisions within that awareness are abundant.
The worlds attain variegation from this abundance of divisions.
No transgression of this explanatory principle is accepted.
items.inference: The diversity of worlds is explained by the multiplicity of divisions within awareness, without invoking any other principle.
items.plain_english: For this very reason, because of the abundance of its divisions, the worlds too become variegated; and no transgression of this explanation is accepted.

rows.grounds: because time has already been criticized

items.question: Can time and space be established as ultimately real principles?
premises: Reality appears as both sequential and non-sequential.
Time has already been refuted as an independent principle.
Space likewise cannot be established as ultimately real by reasoning.
items.inference: Neither time nor space has ultimate reality; their apparent status does not withstand rational examination.
items.plain_english: This reality appears both with sequence and without sequence; but since time has already been refuted, and since the ultimate reality of space cannot be established by reasoning, neither can be taken as ultimately real.

items.question: What could produce the cognition of before and after if no single real principle does so?
premises: No single entity produces the cognition of before and after.
Difference due to limiting conditions is not itself an independently real thing.
A cognition of sequence cannot be grounded in what is not ultimately real.
items.inference: The cognition of before and after cannot be validly postulated as arising from an ultimately real time or from mere adjuncts.
items.plain_english: For no single thing produces the cognition of before and after, and difference based on limiting conditions is not itself a real entity; so how could that cognition be postulated as ultimately grounded?

rows.grounds: whose domain of space and time is created by his own bliss

items.question: How does the supreme Lord relate to distinctions of superiority and to space and time?
premises: Relative superiority is expressed in terms of qualities.
The supreme Lord declared the principle behind such distinctions.
The sphere of space and time is fashioned by the Lord's own bliss.
items.inference: Distinctions of quality and the frameworks of space and time arise within the supreme Lord's own blissful manifestation.
items.plain_english: The supreme Lord, who fashions the sphere of space and time out of his own bliss, declared the basis on which one thing is said to be superior to another by its qualities.

rows.grounds: in the true nature of reality
for those desiring to enter deeply

items.question: Why are absorptions described as threefold in this variegated reality?
premises: The nature of reality is variegated.
Practitioners seek to enter into that reality.
The means of entry differ.
items.inference: Because the means differ for those entering this variegated reality, absorptions are described as threefold.
items.plain_english: Thus, for those who wish to enter into this variegated nature of reality, a threefold division of absorptions has been described, because the means differ.

rows.grounds: the means based on the inert

items.question: What are the three means of absorption and how is the third classified?
premises: The Śāmbhava means is described as methodless.
The next means is based on consciousness.
The Āṇava means is based on the inert and is regarded as manifold.
items.inference: The three means are Śāmbhava, Śākta or consciousness-based, and Āṇava, with the Āṇava admitting many subdivisions.
uncertainties: The text gives cidupāya rather than the explicit name śākta, though the identification is standard in this context.
items.plain_english: The Śāmbhava means is without method; next comes the means based on consciousness; and the Āṇava means, based on the inert, is also regarded as taking many forms.

rows.grounds: in what is conscious or non-material
through the power of the supreme Lord
from nāḍīs, organs, and external supports
its functioning as a means through consciousness

items.question: How can a consciousness-based means operate through apparently inert supports?
premises: Even in the non-inert, an appearance of inertness can arise.
This appearance arises through the power of supreme lordship.
Channels, senses, and external supports can serve as loci for that appearance.
items.inference: Because inert-seeming supports appear within consciousness by the Lord's power, they can function as instruments of the consciousness-based means.
items.plain_english: Even within what is non-inert, an appearance of inertness arises through the power of the supreme Lord, as in the channels, senses, and external supports; therefore these can still function as a means grounded in consciousness.

rows.grounds: the operation of the sense faculties
that is the clear waking state

items.question: What characterizes the waking state in terms of sense activity?
premises: Sense functioning can be taken as the basis of experience.
On that basis there is apprehension of external forms.
This apprehension is clear, present, and repeatedly continuous.
items.inference: The waking state is defined as the clear and repeatedly continuous apprehension of external forms through sense functioning.
items.plain_english: When experience rests on the functioning of the senses and there is a grasping of external forms, that clear and repeatedly continuous condition is the waking state.

rows.grounds: fabrication produced by one's own mental projection
of the limited subject in dissolution
under the power of karma tending toward dissolution

items.question: How is dream distinguished, and what kind of experience belongs to the layākala?
premises: Dream is a construction produced by one's own imagination.
Dream is the reverse of the waking state.
The layākala has experience under the force of karma tending toward dissolution.
items.inference: Dream is internally constructed and opposed to waking, while the layākala's experience is determined by dissolving karma rather than stable manifestation.
items.plain_english: Dream is a construction made by one's own imagination and is the reverse of waking; and the experience belonging to the layākala arises under the force of karma tending toward dissolution, but not in a stable way.

rows.grounds: because there is no night-like obscuration
in the absence of awareness of pleasure etc.
of the limited subject with knowledge obscured

items.question: Why is the layākala's experience unstable, and what defines sleep for the jñānākala?
premises: The layākala's experience would not be stable because there is no night-like obscuration to fix it.
Deep sleep is marked by non-awareness of pleasure and other contents.
For the jñānākala, experience is limited by mere impurity and amounts only to bare experience.
items.inference: Instability in the layākala comes from lack of obscuring fixation, while the jñānākala's sleep-like condition is defined by impurity and mere, contentless experience.
items.plain_english: That experience would not be stable, because there is no night-like obscuration; deep sleep is the non-awareness of pleasure and so on. For the jñānākala, due to mere impurity, there is only bare experience.

rows.grounds: the mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords

items.question: Who abides in the fourth state amid differentiated inert and non-inert entities?
premises: Entities appear as differentiated, both inert and non-inert.
Such differentiation is treated as something made or intended.
In the fourth state, three groups abide: mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords.
items.inference: Within the fourth state, differentiated manifestation is still present, and it is inhabited by the three hierarchic groups of mantra, mantra-lords, and mantra-overlords.
items.plain_english: Inert and non-inert things appear as inherently distinct and differentiated; yet in the fourth state there abide the three groups: the mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords.

rows.grounds: able to admit entry into a portion of Bhairava-consciousness

items.question: When do differentiated entities become non-different?
premises: Entities can become capable of admitting a share of Bhairava-awareness.
When that happens, their separate essence melts away.
With the loss of separate essence, they become non-different.
items.inference: Entities become non-different to the extent that they can receive Bhairava-awareness and their separate essence dissolves.
items.plain_english: To the extent that entities become capable of receiving a share of Bhairava-awareness, their own separate essence melts away and they become non-different by themselves.

items.question: How should the waking state be identified within the fifteenfold scheme?
premises: Entities capable of full non-difference would abide in the state beyond the fourth.
Within the fifteenfold scheme, each level has its own modes.
Whatever form is clear and distinct at a given level is to be regarded as waking.
items.inference: In the fifteenfold analysis, the waking state is defined functionally as whichever form is most clear and manifest at that level.
items.plain_english: They would abide in the state beyond the fourth. In this fifteenfold scheme, whatever form appears clear and distinct should be regarded as the waking state.

items.question: How are dream and deep sleep distinguished from waking in this scheme?
premises: The same form that is clear in waking may appear as unstable.
An unstable appearance of that form is dream.
An unclear appearance is deep sleep.
items.inference: Waking, dream, and deep sleep are distinguished by degrees of clarity and stability in the appearance of the same underlying form.
uncertainties: The final clause 'tat puro 'pi yat' is compressed; its syntactic role is slightly unclear in isolation.
items.plain_english: That same form, when it appears unstable, is dream of that kind; but when it appears unclear, that is deep sleep, including what appears before it.

rows.grounds: the continuity linking the three states
like the string running through a garland

items.question: What is the fourth state in relation to waking, dream, and deep sleep?
premises: Waking, dream, and deep sleep form a triad.
There is a continuity by whose power this triad is held together.
That continuity runs through all differences like a thread through a garland.
items.inference: The fourth state is the unifying continuity that pervades and connects the three states across all differences.
items.plain_english: The continuity by which the three states arise and are held together, like the thread in a garland, should be understood as the fourth state present through all differences.

rows.grounds: radiant with the plenitude of nonduality

items.question: What distinguishes the state beyond the fourth from the fourth state?
premises: The fourth state unifies the triad of waking, dream, and deep sleep.
There is a further state shining with the fullness of nonduality.
That further state melts away all distinctions.
items.inference: The state beyond the fourth is the plenary nondual radiance in which all distinctions are dissolved, and this schema should be applied universally.
items.plain_english: But that which shines with the fullness of nonduality and melts away all distinctions is declared to be the state beyond the fourth; one should apply this understanding everywhere.

rows.grounds: in the case of the layākala subject
waking together with the preceding states
counted as dream and so on
one should follow in all cases

items.question: How should the four-state schema be applied to different levels such as the layākala?
premises: Each level has its own proper form.
What counts as waking, dream, and so on is relative to that level.
The wise should trace the full sequence in every case.
items.inference: The four-state schema is relative and must be applied contextually, with each level's own form determining what counts as waking, dream, sleep, and beyond.
items.plain_english: For the layākala, its own form is waking, and the prior states are counted as dream and so on; the wise person should trace this whole sequence in every case.

rows.grounds: consciousness as the state beyond the fourth

items.question: How do the four states map onto the powers within the one supreme Lord?
premises: Even within the one full Lord, the states can be distinguished.
Consciousness corresponds to the state beyond the fourth.
Bliss corresponds to the fourth, will to the seed-like deep sleep, and further powers follow.
items.inference: The four-state schema is mapped onto the Lord's powers, with cit as beyond the fourth, ānanda as the fourth, and icchā as the seed-ground of deep sleep.
items.plain_english: Even within the one full Lord, consciousness is said to be the state beyond the fourth, bliss is the fourth, and will itself is the seed-ground corresponding to deep sleep.

items.question: How do knowledge and action map onto dream and waking, and what further yogic designations arise here?
premises: Knowledge corresponds to the dream-functioning state.
Action corresponds to the waking state.
In this same framework arise yogic designations such as piṇḍastha and others.
items.inference: The mapping of the Lord's powers to the four states extends to yogic stages, with jñāna as dream-like and kriyā as waking-like.
items.plain_english: Knowledge corresponds to the dream state, and action is remembered as the waking state; in this same context arise the yogic designations beginning with piṇḍastha.

rows.grounds: formed by those who rely on reflective enumeration
because the fourfold structure is present

items.question: Why do additional classifications like sarvatobhadra arise in the expanded scheme?
premises: Classifications such as sarvatobhadra are constructed by discriminative knowers.
In each individual case the fourfold structure is present.
When the scheme is expanded, further subdivisions arise from that fourfold presence.
items.inference: Additional yogic classifications arise because the fourfold structure recurs in every case and is elaborated by reflective analysis.
items.plain_english: Classifications such as sarvatobhadra are constructed by those who rely on discriminative analysis; because the fourfold structure is present in each case, further elaborations arise in the expanded scheme.

rows.grounds: whose universal forms are vividly manifest

items.question: How do multiplicity and unity resolve in the supreme Bhairava?
premises: The scheme can be seen as fourfold in one locus.
It can then be seen as threefold and then as one.
Beyond these reductions stands the one Lord Bhairava, in whom all forms flash forth.
items.inference: The progressive reduction from fourfold to threefold to one culminates in the one Bhairava, who contains and manifests all forms.
items.plain_english: In one place there is fourfoldness, then threefoldness, then oneness; yet the one Lord Bhairava remains, with all universal forms flashing forth within him.
